import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 120

*Reference:*
- [erdosproblems.com/120](https://www.erdosproblems.com/120)
- [St20](http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm1/fm1111.pdf) Steinhaus, Hugo, Sur les distances des points dans les ensembles de measure positive. Fund. Math. (1920), 93-104.
-/

open Set MeasureTheory

namespace Erdos120

/--
There exists a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, dependent on set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$,
of positive measure which does not contain any set of the shape $a * A + b$
for some $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \neq 0$?
-/
def Erdos120For (A : Set ℝ) : Prop := ∃ E : Set ℝ,
  MeasurableSet E ∧ 0 < volume E ∧ ∀ a b : ℝ, a ≠ 0 → ¬ .image (fun x => a * x + b) A ⊆ E

/--
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be an infinite set. Must there be a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
of positive measure which does not contain any set of the shape $a * A + b$
for some $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \neq 0$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 28]
theorem erdos_120 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A : Set ℝ, A.Infinite → Erdos120For A := by
  sorry

/--
Steinhaus [St20] has proved Erdős 120 to be false whenever $A$ is a finite set.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 28]
theorem erdos_120.variants.finite_set {A : Set ℝ} (h : A.Finite) : ¬ Erdos120For A := by
  sorry

end Erdos120

reformulations.difference: The Lean predicate requires a Borel-measurable witness E (`MeasurableSet E` on ℝ), whereas the source uses the usual positive-Lebesgue-measure formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every positive-measure Lebesgue-measurable E contains a Borel subset B with the same measure. Avoiding every nondegenerate affine copy of A is inherited by subsets, so B is also a witness. Conversely, every Borel witness is Lebesgue measurable. This equivalence, with Lebesgue measurability expressed by `NullMeasurableSet E volume`, was proved for every A in the scratch file. Compact-witness and finite-positive-measure-witness equivalences were also proved, confirming that allowing infinite volume does not change the problem.

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. The main quantifiers and nonzero-scale restriction match the source. The finite-set variant correctly negates the avoidance property, equivalently saying that every measurable positive-measure set contains an affine copy. The source still marks the main problem OPEN and records the finite-set case as false, matching both categories. Independent checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile without errors or warnings and cover empty and singleton A, empty/singleton/universal E, zero-scale degeneration, nonzero affine injectivity, and a witness for A = ℝ. These proofs do not use the sorry-backed problem theorems.
